question: Which Constitutional Amendment is commonly called the “Mini-Constitution”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act**, enacted in **1976**, is often referred to as the **"Mini-Constitution"** due to the extensive changes it brought to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was passed during the tenure of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi** during the period of the Emergency in India (1975-1977).
 
• The amendment introduced significant changes to the **Preamble**, the **Fundamental Duties**, and the **Directive Principles of State Policy** (DPSP), among other parts of the Constitution.
 
• The Preamble was amended to include the terms **"Socialist"**, **"Secular"**, and **"Integrity"**, thereby emphasizing the secular and socialist nature of the Indian state.
 
• It added **Fundamental Duties** to the Constitution under **Article 51A**, listing 10 duties for Indian citizens to follow.
 
• The amendment gave precedence to the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** over the Fundamental Rights in case of conflict, altering the balance of constitutional principles.
 
• It introduced provisions like curbing judicial review powers and reducing the authority of the judiciary, thus strengthening the power of the Parliament and the executive.
 
• The 42nd Amendment also extended the tenure of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from **5 years to 6 years**, though this was later reversed by the **44th Amendment Act** in 1978.
 
• ***Hence, the 42nd Amendment is rightly called the "Mini-Constitution" due to its far-reaching changes.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **42nd Amendment Act Details:**

 
 
• The amendment was introduced by the **Indian National Congress** government led by **Indira Gandhi**, and it is one of the most controversial amendments in India's constitutional history.
 
• It was passed during the Emergency period when civil liberties were curtailed, and the opposition was suppressed, which led to criticism of the amendment as being excessively authoritarian.
 
 
 
• **Changes to the Constitution:**
 
 
• The **Preamble** was amended to reflect India's commitment to socialism, secularism, and national integrity.
 
• The addition of **Article 51A** introduced the Fundamental Duties, which include respecting the Constitution, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.
 
• Changes to the judiciary limited its power to review amendments under Article 368, which was later nullified by the **Minerva Mills case (1980)**.
 
 
 
• **Reversal of Provisions:**
 
 
• The **44th Amendment Act (1978)**, passed by the Janata government, reversed some of the authoritarian provisions of the 42nd Amendment, such as the extension of the Lok Sabha's term.
 
• It restored the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), ensuring that Fundamental Rights are not overridden.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of the 42nd Amendment:**

 
 
• **Article 368** was amended to limit judicial review of constitutional amendments.
 
• The concept of the **basic structure doctrine**, introduced by the **Keshavananda Bharati case (1973)**, was challenged but later upheld by the judiciary.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the 42nd Amendment:**
 
 
• It centralized power with the Parliament and the executive, which was seen as a move to undermine federalism and democracy.
 
• It remains a significant example of how constitutional amendments can be used to alter the balance of power in a democracy.
